reason: No cited evidence is provided to support any of the key mechanistic premises, such as the sequential reduction temperatures, the H2 dissociation role of the noble-metal lattice, the kinetic trapping of the fcc phase, or the specific 0.45 eV barrier. The hypothesis relies entirely on unsupported claims.
premises: Noble metal salts (Pt, Ir, Ru) reduce at lower temperatures (~300°C) to form a lattice first
This noble-metal lattice adsorbs and dissociates H2, producing reactive H atoms
Reactive H atoms then reduce less noble metals (Ni, Co, Cu, Fe) which incorporate into the pre-formed lattice
In Pt–Ru systems, an initial Pt-rich fcc phase is kinetically trapped
Secondary heating (400–500°C) overcomes a ~0.45 eV barrier to transform fcc to Ru-rich hcp
